research_question: In adults with overweight or obesity, what is the effect of a smartphone app-based intervention, compared with no intervention or a minimal non-app intervention (e.g., printed materials, paper food diary, usual care), on body weight (kg) at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months, preferably 3-4 months)?
control_label: No intervention or minimal non-app intervention (printed materials, paper food diary, usual care)
outcome_description: Body weight measured in kilograms at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months post-baseline, preferably 3-4 months). One endpoint per study; when a study reports both a follow-up (endpoint) value and a change-from-baseline value for body weight, the change-from-baseline value is preferred. Weight-related outcomes other than body weight in kg (BMI, body fat percentage, waist circumference), and all non-weight outcomes (physical activity, self-efficacy, dietary behaviour, quality of life, etc.) are not extracted or pooled. Medium-term (6 months) and long-term (>=12 months) assessments are excluded.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means the smartphone app group achieved a more favourable body-weight outcome than the no/minimal-intervention control group (i.e., greater weight loss or lower body weight in kg at short-term follow-up).
search_queries: smartphone app weight loss randomized controlled trial adults overweight obesity
mobile phone application weight management intervention trial body weight kilograms
mHealth smartphone application obesity intervention versus usual care weight outcome
inclusion_criteria: Adult participants (mean age >=18 years) who are overweight or obese, or a general adult sample recruited for weight loss/weight management

Evaluates a smartphone app (or app-delivered mobile health program) as the intervention in at least one arm, with a comparison arm receiving no intervention or a minimal, non-app intervention (printed/written materials, paper food diary, usual care, waitlist, or minimal advice)
Reports some quantitative body weight (kg) outcome data at a follow-up point of roughly 3 to <6 months from which an effect size can be derived (means with SDs/SEs/CIs, change scores, t/F statistics)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, protocol, conference abstract without data, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between a treatment and a control condition (single-arm/pre-post only), or both arms receive a smartphone app (app vs. app, or different versions/features of the same app), so the comparator is not a genuine no/minimal non-app intervention
No quantitative outcome data usable to compute an effect size (no means+SDs/SEs, t/F values, proportions, or odds ratios reported or derivable)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g., not a weight-management intervention, paediatric/adolescent-only samples, or body weight in kg not assessed at a 3 to <6 month follow-up)
moderators_to_extract: Comparator type (no intervention/waitlist vs. printed materials or paper diary vs. usual care)
App intervention intensity (standalone app vs. app plus human coaching/counselling contact)
Follow-up length in months (3, 4, or 5 months)
Baseline BMI category of sample (overweight vs. obese)
Endpoint type extracted (change-from-baseline vs. follow-up value)
effect_size_note: Extract one endpoint per study for body weight in kg at the 3 to <6 month assessment (prefer 3-4 months when multiple short-term points exist), preferring change-from-baseline over follow-up values when both are reported. Where multiple eligible app arms exist against a single no/minimal-intervention control, select the primary/most intensive app arm to preserve independence.
